subject.title: feat(slack): support running as a real Slack user (user identity)

question: Should OpenClaw support an opt-in Slack mode that authorizes automation to read and post as a human Slack user through that user’s OAuth token?
rationale: This is an intentional new authority model, not a mechanical bug fix; maintainers must choose its acceptable support and security boundary after the runtime loop defect is corrected and live behavior is shown.

options.title: Approve a bounded opt-in user mode
options.body: Accept the product direction after the self-event guard is fixed and a redacted live Slack proof demonstrates DM/MPIM delivery and self suppression.

options.title: Keep Slack bot-only
options.body: Decline the personal user-OAuth authority model and retain the established Slack app/bot identity surface.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded opt-in user mode
recommendation.body: Accept the product direction after the self-event guard is fixed and a redacted live Slack proof demonstrates DM/MPIM delivery and self suppression.

likelyOwner.reason: Owns the proposed design and its full implementation series, making them the best available routing point for clarifying the intended authority boundary.
